about.intro: Ori Studio aims to be the ultimate workspace for origami design and analysis. It leans heavily on ports of existing origami tools created by the community — the Edit workspace, for instance, is a port of Oriedita to Rust, focused on usability and performance. If you have any suggestions, feel free to <2>open an issue on GitHub</2>.
about.subtitle: A modern shared workspace for designing, editing, and folding origami crease patterns.
about.title: About Ori Studio

boxPleatingStudio.detail: The box-pleated authoring method is a Rust and WebAssembly port of Mu-Tsun Tsai's Box Pleating Studio.
boxPleatingStudio.title: Mu-Tsun Tsai and Box Pleating Studio

oriedita.detail: The crease-pattern editor is a Rust and WebAssembly port of the Oriedita editor (itself a fork of Orihime), including its foldability diagnostics, repairs, and file formats.
oriedita.title: Oriedita

origamiSimulator.detail: The Simulate workspace folds bases into an interactive 3D model using a TypeScript port of Amanda Ghassaei's Origami Simulator.
origamiSimulator.title: Amanda Ghassaei and Origami Simulator

treemaker.detail: TreeMaker's original model code and behavior are the canonical reference for this Rust, WebAssembly, and desktop port.
treemaker.title: Robert J. Lang and TreeMaker 5.0.1

guide.footer: Ori Studio commands are available from the web menubar, native desktop menu, and compact toolbar.
guide.subtitle: A practical map of the current shared browser and desktop app surface.
guide.title: Ori Studio Help

conditions.caption: Conditions are built from the current selection, so select nodes, edges, or paths before adding constraints.
conditions.imageAlt: Conditions pane with paper size, symmetry type, advanced symmetry options, and add-from-selection actions
conditions.step1: Set paper width and height before tuning exact coordinates.
conditions.step2: Choose book, diagonal, or custom symmetry, then use the Design pane mirror tools to author paired leaves.
conditions.step3: Add fixed node, node-on-edge, node-on-corner, paired-node, fixed-length, same-strain, and path conditions from selected parts.
conditions.step4: Use the condition list to inspect, select, or remove constraints as the model evolves.
conditions.summary: The Conditions pane controls paper size, symmetry presets, and selection-based design constraints.
conditions.title: Set Paper, Symmetry, And Conditions

creasePattern.caption: Switch between crease-role and mountain-valley color modes depending on what you need to inspect.
creasePattern.imageAlt: Crease Pattern pane showing a generated crease pattern with color mode controls
creasePattern.step1: Use Color by Crease roles to distinguish axial, gusset, ridge, hinge, and pseudohinge lines.
creasePattern.step2: Crease lines use M/V assignment coloring to show mountains, valleys, flats, and borders.
creasePattern.step3: Use the Edit workspace canvas tools and CP status HUD for crease-pattern selection and diagnostics.
creasePattern.step4: Export SVG or PNG after the crease pattern exists; export FOLD for simulator-ready geometry.
creasePattern.summary: The Edit workspace shows generated or imported crease patterns with role and mountain-valley coloring.
creasePattern.title: Edit Crease Patterns

design.caption: Use the compact viewport controls for zoom, fit, symmetry authoring, and layer visibility.
design.imageAlt: Design pane with tree nodes, edges, labels, leaf circles, zoom controls, and layer controls
design.step1: Select parts directly on the paper; use Shift, Cmd, or Ctrl clicks to build a multi-selection.
design.step2: Click empty paper to add nodes, or select a node and click empty paper to attach a new edge and node.
design.step3: Drag nodes to reshape the tree. Space-drag or the zoom controls help move around larger designs.
design.step4: Toggle paths, leaf circles, labels, and symmetry overlays from the layer menu when the view gets dense.
design.summary: The Design workspace is the main paper surface for selecting, drawing, connecting, dragging, and viewing tree structure.
design.title: Draw And Edit The Tree

files.caption: The File menu keeps project actions, exports, and examples in one place.
files.imageAlt: File menu showing New, Open, Examples, Save, and export commands
files.step1: New returns to the start screen; Open accepts .osf, .tmd, .tmd4, .tmd5, .fold, .cp, .ori, and .orh files.
files.step2: File → Examples loads checked-in starter designs.
files.step3: Save and Save As write Ori Studio project files; use Export for TreeMaker, CP, FOLD, SVG, and PNG formats.
files.step4: Exports become available when the current document has the data each format needs.
files.summary: Use the start screen or the File menu to manage Ori Studio projects and crease-pattern exports.
files.title: Start, Open, Save, Export

folding.caption: Refresh controls regenerate flat-fold artifacts when a crease pattern changes.
folding.imageAlt: Simulator pane showing fold controls and folded geometry
folding.step1: Open Simulate after a crease pattern is built or imported, then drag the viewport to rotate the 3D folded model.
folding.step2: Use the fold slider, play, step, and view controls to inspect the fold motion.
folding.step3: Switch render settings between paper and x-ray views, and toggle faces, edges, and hidden lines.
folding.step4: Generate an Oriedita folded figure directly in the Crease Pattern grid to inspect the flat-folded form.
folding.summary: The Simulate workspace uses the flat-fold artifacts produced from built or imported crease patterns.
folding.title: Simulate The Folded Model

inspector.caption: Selection drives the inspector; change labels, coordinates, edge lengths, and stiffness without leaving the workspace.
inspector.imageAlt: Inspector pane showing editable node label and coordinate fields beside the selected design
inspector.step1: Select a node to edit its label and paper coordinates.
inspector.step2: Select an edge to edit its label, target length, and stiffness, while strain stays report-only.
inspector.step3: Select paths or conditions to review their design metadata.
inspector.step4: When two nodes are selected, the Inspector can select the path between them for path conditions.
inspector.summary: The Design workspace Inspector edits selected nodes and edges and summarizes tree paths and conditions.
inspector.title: Inspect Selection Details

optimize.caption: Ori Studio enables each command only when the document is ready for that step.
optimize.imageAlt: Toolbar showing Optimize Scale and Build CP actions with diagnostics visible
optimize.step1: Optimize Scale fits the tree to the current paper while preserving the selected TreeMaker model semantics.
optimize.step2: Optimize Edges and Optimize Strain are available from the Design menu for deeper optimization workflows.
optimize.step3: Build CP turns an optimized tree into creases, facets, fold directions, and folded-base data.
optimize.step4: Diagnostics report engine readiness, optimization status, feasibility, and crease-pattern build results.
optimize.summary: Optimization and crease-pattern generation run through the shared Design menu, toolbar buttons, and native desktop menu.
optimize.title: Optimize And Build CP

workspace.caption: Reset the pane layout from View or Settings, and choose a theme from the Appearance settings.
workspace.imageAlt: Settings modal and app menu showing theme and layout controls
workspace.step1: Use the left rail or View menu to activate Design, Edit, or Simulate.
workspace.step2: Drag pane headers inside a workspace to reorganize it; Reset Layout restores the current workspace default.
workspace.step3: Settings contains Appearance themes, keyboard shortcuts, and Workspace layout controls.
workspace.step4: Use the Shortcuts settings tab to inspect or rebind file, edit, viewport, and crease-pattern tool commands.
workspace.summary: The app surface is shared between browser and desktop, with web menus, native Tauri menus, workspace layouts, and settings.
workspace.title: Menus, Layout, Settings
